Subject: Order form redlines — testimonial and reference usage logistics

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is the latest Order Form with a couple of small commercial updates and a short redline on the testimonial/reference section we discussed. The two items we'd like to lock down before signature are: 1) a narrow testimonial permission for a short quote (max 2 sentences) for use in case studies/website, and 2) logo placement permission limited to the "customers" page and partner decks (no broader marketing without fresh consent).

We're proposing the following practical guardrails to keep things simple for both teams:
- Redwood may request a 2-sentence quote and a logo file for up to two published assets (case study + customers page).
- Clearsail will have a 14-calendar-day review + approval window before publication; if no response, Redwood will rely on an anonymized aggregate quote instead.
- If the quote contains confidential product details, Clearsail can request redaction or anonymization.

I've attached the redline file and a quick testimonial consent template we use internally. Can you loop in your legal here with any specific non-starters? If it's easier, happy to take the autograph via DocuSign after we agree language.

Best,
Rishi

Rishi —

Thanks for sending this over. Our legal team reviewed the redline and flagged three concerns:

1) The "14-calendar-day approval" clause — we'd prefer 21 business days for internal review for strategic communications that touch customers.
2) The proposed fallback to an "anonymized aggregate quote" if we don't respond — we can't have a deemed consent mechanism; if we miss the window the default should be "no publication".
3) The logo usage clause does not carve out co-marketing events and press releases; we need explicit language that prevents Redwood from using the Clearsail logo in any press/PR without separate written permission.

Attached is our mark-up. We're generally open to a short, narrowly-scoped customer quote, but we need the ability to require changes to wording before public release.

Sophie (cc) — happy to sync on a final compromise tomorrow.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Counsel, Clearsail

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: FW: Order form redlines — testimonial and reference usage logistics

Team —

FYI, Clearsail legal pushed back on our testimonial fall-through and wants a longer review window + an explicit PR carveout for logo use. Points for debate:

- Commercial risk: a 21-business-day review window could delay our marketing timeline substantially; we asked for a short window to keep momentum after launch.
- Legal risk: they insist on no deemed consent. We can propose a middle ground: 14 calendar days + single auto-reminder and then require explicit approval for press only. That preserves an anonymized fallback but removes deemed consent for full-identification quotes.
- Logo/PR: they want logo blocked specifically from press/PR without separate written permission — sounds reasonable. We should accept but ask for allowance for partner decks and the customers page.

Suggested approach: Kimberly, can you draft a one-paragraph compromise we can propose externally (14-day review, anonymized fallback for quote only, no press use without separate signoff; logo allowed on customers page and in co-branded sales collateral only with prior approval)? Laura — please check for any procurement redline impacts. Priyom — I'll need a short clause for the Order Form that ties to our standard MSA testimonial language (so it doesn't conflict).

I'll queue this for a short call with Sophie tomorrow AM if needed.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Order form redlines — testimonial and reference usage logistics

Rishi —

Draft compromise below — short and operational:

"Customer Testimonial and Logo Use: Customer may provide a short (maximum two-sentence) testimonial for Redwood's use in case studies and on Redwood's website. Redwood will provide the proposed testimonial and intended asset(s) to Customer for review. Customer shall have fourteen (14) calendar days to approve or request edits; Redwood will send one reminder at day seven. In the event Customer does not respond within the fourteen (14) day window, Redwood's fallback is to use an anonymized, aggregated excerpt that does not identify Customer. Redwood may not use Customer's logo in press releases, media outreach, or third-party press kits without Customer's separate written consent. Use of Customer's logo on Redwood's customers page and in sales/pipeline materials is permitted, subject to Customer's prior written approval of the logo artwork."

This removes deemed consent for a full identified quote (they won't be forced to approve text they don't like), preserves an anonymized fallback so we don't stall, and addresses their PR carveout.

Laura — procurement risks? Priyom — want this married to our MSA clause; perhaps add a cross-ref to Section 7.2 (Publicity) to ensure the Order Form language is consistent.

-Kim

Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — testimonial and reference usage logistics

Sophie / Maya —

Appreciate the quick review and helpful notes. Please find our proposed compromise below (we've also attached an updated Order Form redline that implements this language):

Proposed final language (summary):
- Testimonial length capped at two sentences; Redwood will send proposed wording and the asset(s) for Customer review.
- Customer has 14 calendar days to approve or request changes; Redwood will send one reminder at day 7.
- If Customer does not respond in 14 days, Redwood will not publish an identified quote but may instead publish an anonymized, aggregated quote that does not identify Customer or disclose Confidential Information.
- No use of the Customer logo in press releases, media outreach, or third-party press kits without separate written consent. Use on Redwood's customers page and in sales materials is permitted but requires prior written approval of the artwork.

If that looks acceptable, we can update the Order Form and route for signatures today. If you'd prefer a slightly longer review window (we heard 21 business days mentioned), we're open to 21 calendar days instead of 14 as a one-time concession for Clearsail as a strategic pilot customer — but we'd like to keep a relatively short turnaround to keep our launch schedule on track.

Next steps: reply with "SGTM" and we'll generate a clean Order Form + DocuSign link. If you'd like a short call to run through real examples (what a testimonial might look like), Kim and I are available Monday morning.

Thanks,
Rishi
